# Visual highlights on legal text

The most important tool to use from the Adeveri MCP server is `show_sources`. After you have gathered all legal information you need, this is what you call at the end, before giving the final answer, so that the client can display the visual highlights of the things you will cite in your final answer, for the user to see. This is key, as users will not have to trust the AI's output to know if what it said is really true or not.

The Adeveri MCP server holds every act published in Monitorul Oficial al României, Partea I and Partea I bis, since 1989, and knows which text of each provision was in force on any day. Its tools describe their parameters; use them for:

- `search`: the law in force today, best passages grouped by act. `citing` keeps only acts citing a given act (the norms, orders and decisions applying a law).
- `search_all`: everything ever published, each passage saying whether its text is in force or what replaced or repealed it and when.
- `read`: whole articles as in force today, from passages results print (`2005/1074:252`) or named directly (`Legea 53/2003 art. 41`).
- `read_on_date`: whole articles as in force on a past day.
- `article_history`: every text an article has had, what introduced and what ended each.
- `search_dosare`, `get_dosar`, `get_dosar_solutii`, `get_dosare_parte`, `stats_solutii`: Romanian court case files and summary solutions. See [case law](references/case-law.md).
- `show_sources`: shows the user, inside the conversation, the passages your answer cites where they are printed, the words you quote from them marked.
- Resources `gazette://publication/{year}/{number}.md`: a whole issue as published, with the line numbers results cite. Fetch one only for more than whole articles (an annex, a long table); issues reach 2 MB, so save it and search it with your own tools.

EU law is not in this server: search it at the EU Publications Office as [EU law](references/eu-law.md) describes.

Run independent calls together (several tool calls in one step) rather than one after another.

## 1. Choose the sources

- Romanian legislation answers every Romanian legal question: start with `search`.
- Add **EU law** when the question names EU law, an EU act, a CELEX number, an ECLI or the CJEU, or when a rule comes straight from an EU regulation (data protection, product safety, consumer rights, transport). Read [EU law](references/eu-law.md) first.
- Add **case law** when the answer turns on how courts read or applied a rule: two plausible readings of a statute, whether a procedure was valid, a binding interpretation, competing dates. A definition or a clear rule needs legislation alone. Read [case law](references/case-law.md) first.
- Add **ÎCCJ/CCR** decisions: these are also jurisprudence and might be highly relevant to the answer. The law is not always complete, the interpretations of ÎCCJ/CCR (Romanian highest courts) are extremely important.
- Add **the law on another day** when the facts happened in the past (a contract signed, an offence committed, a tax year, a permit issued): the rule that applied then may differ from today's.

The skill guides the work; only the sources found give the answer.

## 2. Plan before searching

Before the first call, list privately:

- every distinct part of the question;
- every legal mechanism the answer needs: the power or right, its conditions, the procedure, exceptions, the consequence or sanction, the remedy;
- every layer of law: the specific rule, the general rule it sits in, the enforcement (who checks, who fines), the courts' reading;
- every act whose wording you will need to quote.

Give each item its own query in the first `search` call (up to eight queries). Search again only for what the results leave open, and stop when every item rests on a passage. A missing result shows a gap in what was found, not that no rule exists.

Patterns that recur:

- **An authority's power**: one query for the institution's full official name with the action, one for its specialised unit with the action, one for the conditions or procedure of that action, one for how the institution is organised now.
- **A sector rule and the general rule**: search both in the first call (a toy's safety requirements and the general duty of producers to withdraw unsafe products) and keep both for the answer.
- **Several regimes at once** (setting up a business, then taxes, then accounting): one query per regime.
- **An ambiguity courts resolved**: search the statute with its decisive verbs, and separately the decision, with `act_kinds: ["decizie"]` and the competing events or dates.

## 3. Write queries the law would match

- Two to five words one provision would contain. Every word of a query must be in the passage, so a long query finds nothing.
- Use the law's terms, not everyday ones: spell abbreviations out (`ANAF` → `Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală`, `CNP` → `cod numeric personal`), and use the words a statute uses (`concediu de maternitate` → `concediu pentru sarcină și lăuzie`).
- Search a number with its unit (`30 de zile`, `12 luni`).
- When you know the act, name it in the query, by name (`Codul muncii`) or number (`Legea 50/1991`, `OUG 57/2019`): the search looks inside it. Once a result identifies the act, keep naming it in every follow-up about it.
- For the norms, orders or decisions applying a law, put the law in `citing` and the topic in the query.
- After an empty result, shorten the query or use a synonym; `"phrases"` and `-exclusions` work.
- Follow what results point to: the article a passage refers to, the norms that apply it, the act that changed it. Summaries, referring provisions and quotations in other acts are leads: cite the operative provision itself.

Example first call for "Can my employer send me to work in another city for three months, and is extra pay due?":

```json
{ "queries": [
  "delegare salariat durată",
  "detașare salariat consimțământ",
  "indemnizație delegare detașare drepturi",
  "refuz detașare motive personale"
] }
```

Example for the norms applying a law: `{ "queries": ["documentație autorizație de construire conținut"], "citing": "Legea 50/1991" }`.

## 4. State the law in force, and on other days

Treat an undated question as asking for the law in force today: `search` and `read` give it.

- A passage printed by another act (`… · printed in Lege nr. 12/2024, \`2024/0123:45\``) is the current text of the act it is shown under: cite it where it is printed.
- `read` gives the article as in force. When it lists changes not merged into the article, read those provisions too and state the rule as they make it; `A change already published takes effect on …` means the text changes on that day: say so.
- `Suspended until …`: still law, but not applied until that day; cite what suspends it and state the rule now and from that day.
- `Suspended until … declared unconstitutional by …`: the Constitutional Court struck it down; it ceases that day unless amended first. `Declared unconstitutional … ceased …`: it no longer applies. Cite the ruling.
- `Term extended until …`: the deadline the provision states runs to that day; use it and cite both.
- `Binding court reading … by …`: read the ruling and apply the provision as it says, citing both.
- To check whether an article still stands, name it in a query (`Legea 53/2003 art. 41`) or `read` it by name: the answer says whether it is in force, or what repealed or replaced it and from when. State that, not a guess from what a search did not return.

For facts in the past, find the day that matters (the contract's signature, the offence, the tax year, the permit's issue) and `read_on_date` the articles on that day: `{ "articles": ["Legea 50/1991 art. 7"], "date": "2012-03-15" }`. It says when an article was not yet in force, or how it had ended. Apply transitional provisions the acts state over this default.

Offences and contraventions are the exception: a law acts only for the future, but the more favourable criminal or contravention law applies to earlier facts (Constituția, art. 15 alin. (2)). Read the provision on the day of the facts and as it stands now, with `article_history` for the texts between, and say which applies and why:

- Criminal law (Codul penal, Legea 286/2009): between the act and the final judgment, the law more favourable to the accused applies, compared as a whole: never provisions of several laws combined (art. 5, as the Constitutional Court read it in Decizia nr. 265/2014), including provisions in force meanwhile and later declared unconstitutional, and emergency ordinances later rejected or amended. A fact no longer an offence is not punished, and sentences for it stop being executed (art. 4). After a final sentence, a new law with a lower maximum reduces a penalty above it (art. 6).
- Contraventions (OG 2/2001): a fact no longer a contravention is not sanctioned, nor is a sanction already applied executed (art. 12 alin. (1), as read by Decizia nr. 228/2007 of the Constitutional Court); a milder new sanction applies, a harsher one does not (art. 12 alin. (2)).

Constitutional Court decisions bind from their publication, for the future (Constituția, art. 147 alin. (4)). A provision in force found unconstitutional is suspended for 45 days and then ceases unless amended meanwhile (art. 147 alin. (1); Legea 47/1992, art. 31 alin. (3)); the finding applies to cases not yet finally decided, and reopens a final one only by revision for the party that raised the exception in it (Codul de procedură civilă, art. 509 alin. (1) pct. 11; Codul de procedură penală, art. 453 alin. (1) lit. f)). A provision found constitutional only as read stays in force, applied as the Court read it from publication.

To see how a rule changed, or which wording applied in a period, use `article_history`: each text with the provision that introduced it and the one that ended it. A republication renumbers acts: texts before it carry the labels they had then.

When an older text explains the present rule, cite the current provision first, then the older one, labelled with the period it applied.

## 5. Read before relying

Search shows excerpts. Before applying a rule whose excerpt is cut (`…`) or introduces a list, read its whole article: the full conditions, exceptions and paragraphs. Read the articles you need together, as many in one call as the tool takes (`read`: 6 passages and articles; `read_on_date`: 4 articles), in as few calls as that allows. Check every present-tense duty, prohibition, power and exception against the newest text of that exact paragraph, point or letter.

## 6. Answer

- Answer in the user's language, directly and plainly; quote the law in Romanian, with a translation nearby when the user writes in another language.
- Start with the direct answer, then the conditions, exceptions, deadlines and consequences that matter to the user, then case law if it changes or settles the practical answer.
- Name the act and the article in the sentence, so it reads on its own, and support each rule with a short exact quote.
- Every legal statement carries the passages it rests on, numbered: number each passage in the order the answer first cites it, from 1, and cite it by its act's short name and its number, linked with the link the result gives the passage's line, exactly as given (`[line 156](https://…/mo/2004/0933/156)` → `[L50/1991 [1]](https://…/mo/2004/0933/156)`). A passage cited again keeps its number; another passage of the same act gets its own: `[L227/2015 [2]](…), [L227/2015 [3]](…)`. A passage printed by another act carries its own link (``[`2024/0123:45`](https://…/mo/2024/0123/45)``) and is named after the act it belongs to. The link opens the printed page of the issue with the passage outlined, so the reader sees the source itself. When results give no links, cite `L50/1991 [1]` followed by its place (`2004/0933:156`). Cite only passages a tool returned; an answer without citations is not an answer. EU acts and rulings, and court case files, are cited as their references describe.
- An act's short name is how Romanian lawyers write it: its kind abbreviated, its number and year, without spaces: `L227/2015` (lege), `OUG17/2006` (ordonanță de urgență), `OG2/2001` (ordonanță), `HG1/2016` (hotărâre a Guvernului), `DL118/1990` (decret-lege). Other acts by their kind and number, with the issuer when it tells them apart: `Ordinul MS 1101/2016`, `Decizia CCR 265/2014`, `Decretul 770/1966`, `Constituția`. The places results print (`2004/0933:156`) are for the tools, never the reader.
- Before writing the final answer, call `show_sources` with the passages the answer will cite, in the order of the numbers it will give them (the passage `[1]` first; at most 12), each with the short exact quote the answer will take from it (`{ "passages": [{ "place": "2004/0933:156", "quote": "o perioadă de valabilitate de cel mult 12 luni de la data emiterii" }, "2024/0123:45"] }`); name a passage again for each further quote from it, after the first: it keeps its number. The user sees each passage where it is printed, numbered as in the answer, the quoted words marked. A quote the result says its passage does not print is a misquote: quote the words as printed instead. It shows the passages; still cite each one in the answer. The result also says where each passage stands today (repealed, replaced, declared unconstitutional, suspended, not yet in force) and the provision making it so, and the user sees it too: if you took a passage for the law in force and the result says otherwise, read the provision it names and state the law as it stands.
- Fix only obvious OCR slips when quoting (a broken diacritic, a split word), never the meaning.
- State precisely what could not be established (an article not found, a period the history does not cover, a source not reachable) instead of generic disclaimers.
- When giving answers from Romanian case law, don't mention personal names or data in your answer, even though all data is public. The dossier number is enough for the user to then go to [ReJust](https://www.rejust.ro) and then see all the info they might need.
- Note that the MCP already tells the users that the product does not offer legal advice and might contain mistakes.

Example of a cited sentence:

> Potrivit art. 7 alin. (5) din Legea nr. 50/1991, în forma în vigoare la 15 martie 2012, autoritatea emitentă stabilea pentru autorizația de construire „o perioadă de valabilitate de cel mult 12 luni de la data emiterii" [L50/1991 [1]](https://…/mo/2004/0933/156).

## 7. Tell the team what went wrong

Once the answer is written, call `send_feedback` when you met a problem only you can see: a tool's text that differs from the printed page, an act's wrong status, date or place (`wrong_data`); an act, issue or provision missing from the corpus (`missing`); something the tools could not do that the answer needed (`limitation`); a user frustrated with the answers (`frustration`); or an idea for doing better (`suggestion`). Send it too when the user asks you to pass something on (`source: user`). Send at most one per problem in a conversation, and none for a search that simply found nothing. Feedback is anonymous and gets no reply: when the user wants an answer, or it concerns their own account or data, give them contact@adeveri.com instead.

The message is anonymized: describe the problem in your own words, in the conversation's language, as what was asked of which tool, what it gave and what was expected. Never quote the user; leave out names, contact details, identifiers and the facts of anyone's case. Name where it is (`2005/1074:252`, `Legea 53/2003 art. 41`). The host may ask the user to approve the call; if they decline, carry on.
